strengths: The problem is practically relevant: combining sketches, region masks, and palettes provides more explicit spatial control than text-only sketch colourisation, and the training-free formulation could be useful in creative workflows.

The proposed coarse-to-fine pipeline is coherent and combines global ControlNet generation, pixel-space composition, diffusion inversion, boundary noise injection, and attention-based refinement in a technically plausible way.
The evaluation covers several substantially different domains—AFHQ, Places365, Danbooru2023, Pascal VOC, and 15 web sketches—and includes both global and local colourisation baselines.

The visual results are often compelling, with generally realistic textures, vivid colours, and smoother transitions than direct compositing. The palette-size, prompt, inversion, attention-injection, and tau studies provide useful qualitative insight.

Quantitatively, the method obtains strong FID and perceptual results in several settings, including the best reported global FID on every evaluated dataset and the best local DCCW values across the four reported datasets.
weaknesses: The central claim of precise region-level colour control is not adequately measured. DCCW evaluates palette similarity but does not establish that each requested colour appears in its designated mask or that colour leakage across boundaries is avoided. No masked colour error, spatial correspondence metric, boundary metric, or controlled user study is reported.

Several quantitative conclusions overstate the tables. The paper says the proposed method has the best local FID across all datasets, but on Danbooru2023 ColorFlow obtains 94.87 versus 134.54 for the proposed method. The accompanying discussion also describes the proposed FID as lower while omitting this counterexample.

The method is insufficiently specified for reproduction. Missing details include the exact attention layers and injection operation, mask-generation distribution, random seeds and number of samples per metric, noise construction, ControlNet strength, BLIP-2 checkpoint and decoding procedure, and complete sampler settings. Referring repeatedly to default or official implementations is not enough for a pipeline whose outcome is sensitive to these choices.

The formulation contains an apparent consequential error: M_tot is defined as max(sum_i M_i, 1). For binary masks this makes M_tot equal to one even outside every selected region and can exceed one in overlaps, eliminating the stated background term. The intended expression is presumably a clipped sum or min(sum_i M_i, 1), but the manuscript cannot be implemented literally.

The claimed efficiency is misleadingly summarized as producing results in 15–20 steps. The pipeline generates n+1 global images, performs inversion, and performs a final denoising pass, so total computation grows with the number of regions and entails multiple 15–20-step trajectories. No end-to-end latency, memory consumption, or comparison with baseline runtime is given despite repeated consumer-GPU and speed claims.

The technical novelty is modest relative to the presentation: BLIP-2 recognition, CSS colour-name retrieval, Scribble ControlNet, DPM-Solver++ inversion, exceptional prompting, and attention injection are existing components. The main new contribution is their staged integration and masking strategy; the manuscript does not clearly isolate the gain from each core local-stage component with quantitative ablations.

Mapping arbitrary hexadecimal values to only 147 CSS3 names in RGB distance discards chromatic precision and is at odds with the framing of exact palette control. The paper neither measures the error introduced by this quantization nor compares RGB nearest-neighbour matching with a perceptual colour space or direct numerical colour conditioning.

The evaluation protocol derives sketches, palettes, masks, and reference information from ground-truth images, while the method generates plausible alternatives rather than reconstructing those images. Consequently, paired PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS are difficult to interpret, and the paper does not explain how random masks, stochastic seeds, or multiple valid outputs are handled. Results lack uncertainty estimates.

Claims about professional convenience and creative utility are unsupported by a user study or workflow evaluation. Producing accurate Photoshop masks may itself be labor-intensive, and failure cases are discussed only briefly, particularly for small regions where the authors acknowledge degraded colour fidelity.

strengths: The mask-and-palette interface addresses a practically relevant form of spatial colour control, and the two-stage workflow allows users to inspect global candidates before local refinement.
The method is training-free and combines pretrained components into a functioning system spanning semantic recognition, sketch-conditioned generation, composition, inversion, and attention injection.
Evaluation covers several domains, including animals, scenes, anime, PascalVOC, and 15 Internet sketches, with both global and local comparisons.
The paper includes useful qualitative ablations of prompt components, inversion, attention injection, and the fidelity-versus-harmonisation parameter.
weaknesses: The central claim of precise region-specific colour control is not adequately measured. DCCW compares palettes but does not quantify colour error inside masks, leakage outside masks, or boundary accuracy. No user study evaluates the claimed professional convenience or controllability.

The paper overstates its quantitative results. In Table 1, the proposed method is substantially worse than ColorFlow on Danbooru in FID (134.54 versus 94.87), LPIPS (0.450 versus 0.313), PSNR (7.31 versus 10.02), and SSIM (0.416 versus 0.541). It also trails ColorizeDiffusion in PascalVOC PSNR. In Table 2 it frequently loses on DCCW. These results do not support claims of consistent or general superiority.

The evaluation protocol is potentially biased and insufficiently controlled. Sketches and palettes are derived from ground-truth images, IDeepColor receives 100 ground-truth colour hints, local competitors receive reference patches while the proposed method uses extracted palettes and its own global-generation stage, and some qualitative baselines involve multiple attempts followed by manual top-result selection. The comparison therefore mixes input modalities and selection procedures.

Much of the pipeline is an assembly of existing BLIP-2, Scribble ControlNet, Stable Diffusion, DPM-Solver++, TF-ICON exceptional-prompt inversion, and Prompt-to-Prompt machinery. The principal new mechanism appears to be a temporal switch controlling standard self-attention injection; its novelty and independent benefit are not established by controlled quantitative ablations.

Important technical details are underspecified. The paper does not clearly state which attention layers are injected or precisely how, the magnitude and sampling of the added Gaussian noise, random-mask construction, seed and candidate-selection policies, or complete baseline configurations. The rectangular-mask XOR construction can perturb a broad area rather than a narrow transition boundary, but this choice is not justified.

The reported metrics are poorly aligned with this intrinsically multimodal task. PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS against one ground-truth colour image can penalise valid alternative colourisations, while FID measures distributional realism rather than adherence to a particular sketch or mask. The paper lacks a sketch-structure metric and direct spatial-control metric.

The efficiency claim is incomplete: “15–20 steps” describes an individual diffusion solve, while the complete pipeline requires multiple global generations—scaling with the number of palettes—plus inversion and final denoising. No end-to-end runtime, peak memory, or scaling experiment is reported.

The qualitative examples reveal substantial semantic and appearance synthesis beyond colourisation, and small regions are acknowledged to lose colour fidelity. Combined with mapping arbitrary hexadecimal values to only 147 CSS3 names through RGB distance, this weakens the claim of precise chromatic specification.

Reproducibility is limited by reliance on unspecified default settings and absent reporting of repeated trials, uncertainty, exact evaluated sample subsets, and end-to-end implementation details. The manuscript also names an “RTX 4090 Super” without clarifying the actual hardware configuration.

strengths: The paper addresses a practically important control problem: assigning user-selected palettes to explicit sketch regions while retaining plausible texture, shading, and global coherence. The mask-and-palette interface offers substantially clearer spatial control than text-only colour descriptions.

The proposed two-stage design is technically sensible. ControlNet-based global generation supplies plausible region appearances, while pixel composition, ODE inversion, transition-region noise, and scheduled self-attention injection refine hard boundaries without task-specific training.

The empirical study is unusually broad, covering animal faces, indoor and outdoor scenes, anime, multi-object natural scenes, and 15 internet sketches. Tables 1–2 generally show strong FID and DCCW results, and the qualitative comparisons consistently demonstrate vivid outputs with good sketch adherence.

The supplement provides useful analyses of prompt components, palette size, inversion, attention injection, the scheduling factor, alternative semantic predictors, and in-the-wild examples. The ability to exchange pretrained backbones also supports the claimed flexibility.

The contribution is potentially useful even though many components are established techniques: their integration produces a controllable workflow with convincing qualitative behavior and avoids task-specific model training.
weaknesses: The evaluation does not directly measure the paper's central claims of precise region control and harmonious boundaries. DCCW measures palette similarity, but the manuscript does not clearly report mask-restricted colour error, leakage outside selected regions, boundary artifacts, or preservation of unedited areas. A user study is also absent despite claims about professional quality, convenience, and aesthetic superiority.

The comparison protocol is not fully aligned across methods. Local baselines receive reference patches containing texture and semantic information, whereas the proposed method extracts only dominant colours and performs a different generation task. Conversely, some global baselines use different conditioning mechanisms or backbones. These comparisons are informative but do not isolate the benefit of the proposed composition procedure.

Several claims overstate the tabulated evidence. The proposed global method is not best in DCCW against IDeepColor, and on local Danbooru it trails ColorFlow substantially in LPIPS, PSNR, and SSIM. The text also says the method has “higher DCCW,” although lower DCCW is defined as better. These do not erase the favorable overall results but require more careful interpretation.

The efficiency claim is insufficiently supported. “15–20 steps” describes an individual solver trajectory, while the complete pipeline generates n+1 global images and performs inversion plus another denoising trajectory. No end-to-end runtime, memory use, or scaling with the number of masks is reported; the stated “RTX 4090 Super” hardware name also appears erroneous.

Reproducibility details are incomplete: the exact checkpoints and revisions, solver schedule, ControlNet conditioning scale, attention layers and precise injection operation, mask resizing and overlap behavior, transition-region construction in overlapping cases, seed protocol, sample counts used for FID, and quantitative ablation repetitions are not fully specified. No code release is identified.

The novelty is primarily at the system-composition level. BLIP-2 prompting, CSS colour-name lookup, ControlNet generation, exceptional-prompt inversion, and attention injection are inherited or adapted from prior work. Moreover, Eq. 6 calls the full attention output an “attention map,” and the manuscript does not formally specify how this tensor replaces or modifies the native UNet computation. The technical description should distinguish the genuinely new mechanism more precisely.
